about: Fixed before any code that meets them (SANDBOX_INSTRUMENTS.md, "Orbit geometry"). A criterion that fails is reported with its numbers; no bound here is moved, widened or made conditional after a result.

a.what: orbitGeometry's a, e, periapsis direction, both apsis points, both foci and its 240 curve points against an independent eccentric-anomaly construction of the same orbit
a.note: closed formulas in double precision; an error above 1e-9 of a is a bug, not round-off

b.what: every curve point's sum of distances to the two foci equals 2a

c.stepping: as the page steps it: frameAdvance(1/60 s), substepPlan, one updatePhysics per piece (the 445 reference runner's driver)
c.span: one anomalistic period of the ellipse drawn at the start
c.what: max over every step of the shortest distance from the body to the ellipse drawn at the start (fixed in the world), divided by a
c.reason: a first-order step at about 7,300 steps an orbit (INFERRED)
c.stop: run the unmodified integrator first; if it misses, stop and report an integrator finding; never widen

d.what: one-way circle: a star of mass 1 and a planet of mass 0.1 at r = 100, speed 0.1 tangential, G = 1 (the engine's gravitational_constant set to 1 for this world), mutual gravity off

engine.source: the second-order form tests/fixtures/reference-cases/thresholds.json commits for a circular start (R1), applied to the radius, which on a circle moves with the energy to first order

e.what: no curve, and the reason in words, where the force is not inverse-square over the orbit
cases: two reciprocal stars of mass 1 and 0.1 at r = 1, softening length 5, G = 1
the same pair at r = 10 at apoapsis with a point-mass periapsis of 1.111 (e = 0.8)

sizes.what: solar-system as built: drawn Sun to Earth radius ratio before the marker floor
